verses.text: Everyone should submit to the governing authorities. No authority exists except by God's permission, and the authorities that do exist have been established by God.
So whoever resists authority is resisting what God has established, and those who resist will bring judgment on themselves.
Rulers aren't a threat to people who do good, but to those who do evil. Do you want to have no fear of the authorities? Do what's good, and they'll commend you,

because the ruler is God's servant for your good. But if you do evil, be afraid: the ruler doesn't carry the sword for nothing. They serve God as an agent of justice, bringing judgment on the wrongdoer.
So you should submit, not only to avoid punishment but also for the sake of your conscience.
That's also why you pay taxes: the authorities are God's servants, continually carrying out their duties.
Give everyone what you owe them: taxes to the tax collector, customs duties where they're owed, respect to those due respect, and honor to those due honor.
Don't owe anyone anything, except the debt of loving one another. Whoever loves their neighbor has fulfilled the law.
The commands—don't commit adultery, don't murder, don't steal, don't covet—and any other command are summed up in this: ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’
Love doesn't harm a neighbor. So love fulfills the law.
Do this because you know what time it is: it's time to wake up. Our salvation is nearer now than when we first believed.
The night is almost over, and the day is close. So let's throw off the works of darkness and put on the armor of light.
Let's live honorably, as people do in the daylight—not in wild parties and drunkenness, not in sexual immorality and reckless behavior, and not in fighting and jealousy.
Instead, clothe yourselves with the Lord Jesus Christ, and don't make plans to satisfy your human nature and its desires.
